956: The size of any minimal generating set of a homogeneous ideal is
957: well-defined. This is implied by the following well-known fact:
958: Proposition 4.11 .
959: Let R be a commutative ring, and \Lambda=\oplus_{n\geq 0}\Lambda_{n} a graded, connected R-algebra, meaning that \Lambda_{0}=R and \Lambda_{i}\Lambda_{j}\subset\Lambda_{i+j}. Let M be a
960: graded \Lambda-module, with degrees bounded below, meaning that
961: M=\oplus_{n\geq N}M_{n} for some N\in{\mathbb{Z}}, and \Lambda_{i}M_{j}\subset M_{i+j}.
962: Then a set of homogeneous elements \{m_{i}\}_{i=1}^{t} generate M as a \Lambda-module
963: if and only if their images \{\bar{m_{i}}\}_{i=1}^{t} span M/\Lambda_{+}M as a R-module.
964: In particular, \{m_{i}\}_{i=1}^{t} form a minimal \Lambda-generating set with respect to
965: inclusion for M if and only if \{\bar{m_{i}}\}_{i=1}^{t} form a minimal R-spanning
966: set for M/\Lambda_{+}M.
967: In our setting, the well-definedness follows by setting
968: \Lambda=\oplus_{n\geq 0}\Lambda_{n} to be the graded ring of
969: symmetric functions with {\mathbb{Z}} coefficients and setting
970: M=J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}, so that the {\mathbb{Z}}-module M/\Lambda_{+}M
971: is a finitely generated abelian group.
972: Thus we conjecture that this abelian group M/\Lambda_{+}M requires
973: \binom{a+b}{a} generators, and in fact, we suspect that
974: M/\Lambda_{+}M\cong{\mathbb{Z}}^{\binom{a+b}{a}}. So far a proof
975: has eluded us.
